specialistReviews.finding: Source lock/index is not concurrent Postgres proof; service-role can still spoof author or disable triggers.
specialistReviews.resolution: Require disposable Postgres dual-connection race and effective actor grants tests before release.

specialistReviews.finding: Canonical partial unique index can fail when occupied target already has duplicates.
specialistReviews.resolution: No target apply; read-only duplicate inventory and remediation before migration.

specialistReviews.finding: Single high-risk DB-schema migration qualifies for isolated 5/5 release.
specialistReviews.resolution: One SQL+manifest+neutral test, exact F14 HEAD, no Preview.

specialistReviews.finding: Advisory transaction locks could impact autosave latency under load.
specialistReviews.resolution: Require performance/retry concurrency rehearsal, no production changes now.

challenge.scenario: Two browser tabs simultaneously auto-save their first reply draft for the same instance, signed-in author and customer thread.
challenge.finding: Both inserts can pass an application-level existence check and create duplicate drafts before either transaction commits.
challenge.resolution: Preserve the canonical pg_advisory_xact_lock scoped to instance/author/thread and partial unique index; a two-session Postgres race test must assert one conflict.

challenge.scenario: Two distinct support employees each start a reply draft to the same customer support conversation.
challenge.finding: A singleton keyed only by tenant and thread would incorrectly block legitimate separate authors from drafting independent replies.
challenge.resolution: Keep author_user_id in both advisory hash construction and partial unique index and require real target positive two-author acceptance.

challenge.scenario: One support employee edits reply drafts for two different customer threads in one tenant.
challenge.finding: A singleton key missing thread_id would cause unrelated reply drafts to collide or serialize incorrectly.
challenge.resolution: Require distinct thread_id in lock hash and uniqueness columns, then test two-thread separate insert acceptance.

challenge.scenario: Two isolated webshop instances happen to reference equal user UUID and thread UUID due to imported or fixture data.
challenge.finding: Cross-tenant draft uniqueness could leak or deny another tenant if instance_id is omitted from singleton key.
challenge.resolution: Preserve instance_id in advisory lock text and unique index; use tenant-isolated test fixtures with both instances.

challenge.scenario: A user creates several ordinary new_email drafts with NULL thread_id while also composing reply drafts.
challenge.finding: A broad unique index could incorrectly constrain unrelated outbound draft content and block legitimate new-email workflows.
challenge.resolution: Trigger must early-return for draft_type not reply or NULL thread_id, and index must be partial WHERE reply and thread_id IS NOT NULL.

challenge.scenario: A legitimate author updates the subject/body of their existing reply draft without changing the thread/tenant/author identity.
challenge.finding: An existence check that matches the updated row itself would raise OFFICE_DRAFT_CONFLICT and make routine autosaves impossible.
challenge.resolution: Canonical WHERE d.id<>new.id must exclude same row; prove a valid status/content UPDATE via actual disposable Postgres.

challenge.scenario: An occupied staging database already contains duplicate reply drafts with the same tenant, author and thread created before this migration.
challenge.finding: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX will fail during rollout or lock critical Office tables if legacy duplicate records are not identified.
challenge.resolution: Keep production/staging unchanged and require read-only duplicate group inventory, remediation strategy and migration-window assessment.

challenge.scenario: A privileged background worker passes a forged author_user_id as it inserts a reply draft under service_role.
challenge.finding: A uniqueness key scoped to that forged UUID does not authenticate the real caller and could impersonate another employee.
challenge.resolution: Keep actor/session binding and effective privilege role verification as separate release blockers; never treat source hash tests as full identity proof.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The 0061 draft optimistic revision RPC protects updating an existing draft, but two tabs concurrently creating the FIRST reply draft for one (instance, author, customer thread) may each generate a new ID/revision=1. Canonical 20260909203242 must follow 0061 in Fresh Install: it serializes first reply draft creation via transaction-scoped advisory lock, raises OFFICE_DRAFT_CONFLICT when a competing reply draft exists and enforces a partial unique index. Non-reply drafts and different authors/threads must remain unaffected; no real Postgres concurrency execution claimed.
observableOutcomes: Append 0062 full-byte canonical draft singleton SQL with SHA256 source provenance.
A BEFORE INSERT and UPDATE-of-identity trigger takes tenant/author/thread hashed advisory transaction lock on reply draft.
Existing reply draft per tenant-author-thread raises OFFICE_DRAFT_CONFLICT instead of creating a second one.
Partial unique index enforces same invariant in database, excluding new_email and NULL thread_id cases.
Customer baseline guard validates 63 ordered migrations snapshot-reviewed, no target Fresh Install proof hash.
No actual concurrency/actor/bypass proof, advanced Pro SQL or DB target write.
